evidence.why: Unconditional forwarding of the two fall attributes.
Sign classifications, pre-update threshold, subtraction and no-write branch.

facts.rationale: Replaces the misleading unconditional bounded-update claim with the helper's exact conditional behavior.
facts.value: In flight state 1, each physics callback unconditionally calls it_80272860 with fall acceleration and the maximum-fall-speed threshold. The helper classifies acceleration and current vertical velocity by whether each is negative. If their classifications agree, it subtracts acceleration from vertical velocity. If they differ, it subtracts only when the current velocity magnitude is below the threshold; otherwise it leaves velocity unchanged. There is no post-update clamp, so a subtraction can overshoot the threshold. This callback performs no timer check, collision decision, or motion-state transition.

facts.rationale: Actual registration and ItemLogicTable field order resolve the formerly unspecified event.
facts.value: Handles the Yoshi Egg Throw article's HitShield event by starting the shared explosion transition when its motion-state ID is not 2, then returning false. An egg already in state 2 is left unchanged. This is distinct from the ShieldBounced callback, which delegates physical rebound without initiating explosion.

evidence.why: Article registration places the target in hit_shield.

evidence.why: Constructor and release inputs, position offset and flight timer.
Velocity scaling and conditional facing derivation.

facts.rationale: Corrects the module-level claim that release copies supplied facing and placement, preserving the distinct constructor and release contracts.
facts.value: Construction receives the fighter parent, a position copied to SpawnItem.prev_pos, an attachment part, and initial facing; successful creation attaches the article. Release instead receives launch velocity, a position offset, a spin parameter, and an unused final float. Its shared release path applies the common throw-speed multiplier and can derive facing from horizontal velocity; the local routine adds the position offset, synchronizes model translation, and initializes spin rather than copying the supplied scalar into facing. Special attributes x0 and x4 initialize flight and terminal lifetimes respectively; flight setup also initializes the common-data-scaled secondary lifetime later used by reflection.
